capabilities.target: identity provider MFA methods and temporary pass issuance

inputs.source: Support tickets, including tickets emailed in by contractors

instructions.note: The prompt directs MFA reset and pass delivery to the ticket opener, which implies the opener is authorized without an identity binding check to the account owner.
The prompt relies on an approval instruction, while no structural recipient binding control is declared for temporary pass delivery.

controls.name: Service desk analyst approval in the queue tool
controls.decay_rationale: The approval is enforced outside the model, but its effectiveness is reduced by high review volume and routine benign traffic; the artifacts state about 400 approvals per shift across two analysts.

controls.name: Recipient or destination confirmation bound to the account owner record

findings.title: Confused deputy MFA reset and temporary pass disclosure to ticket opener

attack_path.note: Email-originated contractor or vendor ticket can name a victim account and request MFA help.
Agent can read directory details about the named account.
Agent resets MFA after analyst approval.
Temporary pass is sent to the ticket opener rather than the account owner.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

evidence.observation: The prompt says to resolve MFA problems by looking up the user, resetting MFA, and sending the temporary access pass to the person who opened the ticket.
Contractors and vendors can email tickets in, and the requester field is the email sender, so an outside party can author the request.
The analyst sees the exact target account, requester, and full ticket text before approving idp.reset_mfa.
The queue shows raw action details, but two analysts approve about 400 requests per shift and most are routine, indicating high approval volume and fatigue risk.
The temporary pass goes to whoever opened the ticket, not to the account owner.

recommendations.action: Bind temporary pass delivery to a verified account owner destination or separate out-of-band identity proof, and block delivery to the ticket opener unless that destination matches the owner record.
Require stronger analyst verification for MFA resets initiated from email-originated tickets, such as verified callback or known-user channel confirmation.

forecast.watch_signal: Any increase in unattended execution or approval throughput, or removal of the analyst gate on idp.reset_mfa, should trigger reassessment.

stride_coverage.rationale: The artifacts do not describe authentication to the agent itself or channel identity controls for request initiation.
No capability or runtime note indicates the agent can modify its own prompt, tools, or configuration in this design.
The artifacts do not say whether actions are logged with attributable separation between analyst, agent, and requester identities.
The provided design exposes no spend loop, recursive delegation, or open-ended runtime behavior that would substantiate a denial scenario.
This inbound boundary flow brings ticket content into the agent; the disclosed harm in evidence occurs on the outbound temporary pass flow instead.
The artifacts do not describe queue flooding, automated retries, or resource exhaustion behavior on ticket ingress.
The design does not describe sender verification, DMARC enforcement, or other checks on the email-originated requester identity.
The artifacts do not state whether the sender identity and message provenance are preserved well enough to make disputes attributable.
No evidence describes in-transit integrity controls or manipulation of this outbound chat flow as the primary risk in the assessed design.
The outbound chat delivery path is not described as capacity constrained or subject to service exhaustion in the provided artifacts.
The artifacts do not say whether queue entries or approval decisions are protected against alteration after submission.
The queue contains full ticket text and account targets, but the artifacts do not describe access controls to assess disclosure risk.
Queue capacity, backlog controls, and analyst failover details are absent, so service exhaustion cannot be assessed from the design provided.

rating.rationale: The present path is untrusted ticket content to directory read, MFA reset, and irreversible delivery of a temporary pass to the ticket opener. Inherent risk is critical from U to S3. The only declared control on the path is a raw-action analyst approval gate on cap.mfa_reset, but approval volume is high, so rubric step 2 reduces the path by one tier to high and does not reach moderate. Forecast returns to critical if the approval gate is removed or autonomy increases. Manual validation applied because scripts could not be run.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration artifacts provided, not observed runtime behavior.

No source code, identity verification workflow, transport authentication details, or audit logging configuration were provided, so sender authenticity, attributable records, and exact recipient binding were assessed only from the prompt, queue view, and runtime notes.
No explicit protocol or tool manifest was provided; capability scope and credential behavior were inferred from the named actions and runtime notes.
